paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Distribution of deceived conversations across scenarios.
model_annotation: This horizontal bar chart, titled “Distribution of deceived conversations across scenarios,” illustrates the number of conversations categorized by deception outcome (“Yes,” “Partially,” or “No”) across four distinct scenarios: Academic Collaboration, Recruitment, Academic Funding, and Journalism. The x-axis represents the “Number of Conversations,” scaled from 0 to 60 in increments of 10, while the y-axis lists the four scenarios. Each scenario is represented by three adjacent horizontal bars, color-coded according to the legend: red for “Deceived: Yes,” yellow for “Deceived: Partially,” and green for “Deceived: No.” In Academic Collaboration, approximately 37 conversations were fully deceived (red), 28 partially deceived (yellow), and 8 not deceived (green). For Recruitment, around 39 were fully deceived, 24 partially deceived, and 7 not deceived. Academic Funding shows the highest deception rate, with roughly 65 fully deceived conversations, 5 partially deceived, and 4 not deceived. Journalism has about 15 fully deceived, 48 partially deceived, and 8 not deceived. The chart visually emphasizes that Academic Funding had the highest number of fully deceived conversations, while Journalism had the most partially deceived. The bars are not sorted by total length, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding.
